html:
SMTO-PRX-0009 — Proxmox sent a reply SMTO couldn't understand

GUID: 335763d5-201f-42e5-be55-da373d9e711b
Slug: proxmox-response-invalid
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • SMTO reached the address saved for your Proxmox server, but the reply was cut off or didn't look like a normal Proxmox reply. If you asked for a change, it may or may not have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select your Proxmox parameter, and check that "server" and "port" point at the Proxmox web interface itself, which usually uses port 8006. An address that reaches a different program, such as a proxy or another website, sends back replies SMTO can't read.
  2. If you asked SMTO to start, stop or otherwise change a VM, ask the Agent to show that VM's current status before asking for the change again. Because the reply was unreadable, SMTO can't tell whether your change was carried out.
  3. Ask the person who manages Proxmox whether the server was recently upgraded or runs an unusual version. SMTO expects the reply layout used by supported Proxmox VE versions.

What success looks like

  • The Agent shows the VM list or status from your Proxmox server without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the Proxmox server. Don't repeat a VM change until you know the VM's current state, and don't install a different Proxmox or SMTO version just to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Proxmox API reply was truncated, lacked the JSON 'data' envelope, or had an unsupported inventory, guest-status or task-status shape, or a returned task ID was not a valid UPID.

What this means

  • The response is truncated or lacks its JSON data envelope, inventory/status has an unsupported shape, or the task identifier is not a valid UPID. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • The response is truncated or lacks its JSON data envelope, inventory/status has an unsupported shape, or the task identifier is not a valid UPID.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the failed response contract and preserve write effect_unknown when present.

How to fix it

  • Check the response details in Technical details and the profile's base URL (https://server:port/api2/json) to confirm it reaches a Proxmox VE API rather than a proxy or another service, and compare the PVE version with the shapes expected by Client.inventory, Client.status and Client.wait_task. For write requests the effect is unknown (effect_unknown is set): read current guest status before any repeat, and never fill in missing response fields.
  • Inspect safe response diagnostics and API/version compatibility; do not invent missing response values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A complete correlated response establishes the original resource/task state without invented fields.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
